notes.text: No .github/workflows directory was present at d4a2c8d. Existing notes record a historical package smoke test and Linux service validation; those outcomes must not be presented as a current automated check. The owner explicitly reaffirmed reusable distribution as an experiment on 2026-09-05.

problem: The checkout has pnpm check and build scripts but no checked-in GitHub Actions workflow. Repeating broad manual validation costs time, and a passing source checkout does not prove a new user can run the packed CLI and dashboard.

risk.rollback: Revert the focused implementation change without changing existing project configuration or unrelated runtime ownership.

scope: Add one small CI workflow using the supported pnpm check and build commands, a pinned package-manager setup, and cancellation of superseded runs.

Pack the built artifact and install it into an isolated prefix outside the source tree. Smoke-test CLI discovery, static dashboard assets, and an isolated controller with fixture repositories and temporary ports/state.

Exercise the documented install -> register repository -> inspect/claim through MCP path without printing credentials. Preserve shell-free commands and no automatic dependency installation inside managed projects.

Keep CI independent of the owner's filesystem, local Hub checkout, running service, systemd policies, credentials, and private repositories. Any backlog validation step must use a pinned, portable validator setup.

Use Linux for the first repeatable smoke path. Add macOS coverage only for supported behavior that needs it; service-manager integration validation remains in its existing item. Do not publish npm packages or change installed services as a CI side effect.
source: Repository assessment and owner direction on 2026-09-05
title: Automate portable checks and a clean package smoke test
validation: Run checks/build/package installation in an isolated environment without access to the checkout's dependencies or state, and verify the executable serves packaged assets.
Verify missing assets, a failed check, a spawned fixture left alive, or failed cleanup makes the job fail; never label a restarted process as a completed check.
Inspect the package and CI output for accidental state, credentials, logs, or host paths. Document one finite smoke command usable locally and in CI.
value: The owner avoids repeating installation checks, and other developers can try the experiment without reproducing the owner's machine.
